precepts.text: Amaziah did right in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart, explaining why he was not counted like David.
precepts.point: When the kingdom was confirmed, he slew the servants who had killed his father, but did not slay their children, according to the law of Moses that every man is put to death for his own sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 14: Amaziah, the Imperfect Heart, and Jeroboam II

precepts.why:
Chronicles gives the same king, twenty and five years old, reigning twenty and nine years in Jerusalem, his mother Jehoaddan of Jerusalem. And it says plainly what Kings means: “he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart.”

That explains the words in Kings, “yet not like David his father.” Amaziah did right, but he did not serve with a perfect heart, and so he was not counted like David.

precepts.text: The parallel account: Amaziah slew the servants that killed his father, but not their children, according to the law of Moses.
precepts.point: He slew the murderers but he did not slay their children, because it is written in the law of Moses that the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin. This is a foundational law: a man answers for his own sin, not for another man's.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

precepts.why:
The parallel account in Kings tells the same thing: “as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, that he slew his servants which had slain the king his father. But the children of the murderers he slew not.”

Amaziah did this “according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, wherein the Lord commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall be put to death for his own sin.”

So in this he did “that which was right in the sight of the Lord”, even though it was “not with a perfect heart.” He punished the murderers, and kept the law by sparing their children.

precepts.text: Every man shall be put to death for his own sin, not for the sin of his father or his child.
precepts.point: He slew the murderers but he did not slay their children, because it is written in the law of Moses that the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin. This is a foundational law: a man answers for his own sin, not for another man's.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

precepts.why:
This is the law Amaziah followed, straight from Moses: “The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.”

It is a foundational law. A man answers for his own sin, not for the sin of his father or his child. That is why Amaziah slew the servants that killed the king his father, “But he slew not their children”, doing “as it is written in the law in the book of Moses.”

precepts.text: The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of Ahab's prophets to draw him to his fall; the king who trusts false counsel over the true prophet is set up for destruction.
precepts.point: The Most High sent a prophet who asked why he sought after gods that could not even deliver their own people out of his hand. This is why counsel is important. The prophet was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him and told him to forbear, be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said the Most High had determined to destroy him because he had done this and had not hearkened to counsel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came forth and said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.” And the Lord said, “Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.” The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of Ahab’s prophets to draw him to his fall.

The king who trusts false counsel over the true prophet is set up for destruction. That is Amaziah. The Most High gave him the victory over the children of Seir, and he responded by grabbing the idols of the people he had just defeated: he “brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.” That is the divided heart in action.

This is why counsel is important. The prophet asked him, “Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?” He was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him: “Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten?” Be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said, “I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.”

precepts.text: It was counted unlawful for a man that is a Jew to keep company with one of another nation; the split between the kingdoms ran that deep.
precepts.point: Joash took Amaziah, came to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem four hundred cubits. He took all the gold and silver and the vessels found in the house of the Most High, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria. The two kingdoms had real animosity, calling each other another nation, brother stealing the vessels out of his own brother's temple.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

precepts.why:
Peter said, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation.” It was counted unlawful for a man that is a Jew to keep company with one of another nation, and the split between the kingdoms ran that deep.

The two kingdoms had real animosity, calling each other another nation. Amaziah, lifted up after he had “smitten the Edomites”, sent to Joash king of Israel, “Come, let us see one another in the face.” Joash answered with the parable of “The thistle that was in Lebanon” and “the cedar that was in Lebanon”, and told him, “thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt”.

“But Amaziah would not hear; for it came of God, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought after the gods of Edom.” “Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent.” Joash “brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits”, and took “all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God”, the treasures of the king’s house and the hostages, and returned to Samaria. Brother stealing the vessels out of his own brother’s temple.

points: Amaziah began to reign at twenty and five years old and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, but not with a perfect heart. As soon as the kingdom was established he slew the servants that had killed his father the king.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: He slew the murderers but he did not slay their children, because it is written in the law of Moses that the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin. This is a foundational law: a man answers for his own sin, not for another man's.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Amaziah gathered Judah and Benjamin, numbered them from twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand choice men able to go to war. He also hired a hundred thousand mighty men out of Israel for a hundred talents of silver.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: A man of the Most High came and told him not to let the army of Israel go with him, for the Most High was not with Israel, with all the children of Ephraim. Because of the sin of Ephraim the Most High had cast them off and was not dealing with them, so their help would only bring defeat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: When Amaziah asked what to do about the hundred talents he had already paid, the prophet told him the Most High is able to give him much more than that. Amaziah obeyed, separated the army of Ephraim to go home, and they went home in great anger.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Amaziah strengthened himself, led his people to the valley of salt, and smote ten thousand of the children of Seir, and cast down another ten thousand from the top of the rock. But he brought back the gods of the children of Seir, set them up to be his own gods, bowed to them, and burned incense to them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: This is the divided heart in action. The Most High gave him the victory, and he responded by grabbing the idols of the people he had just defeated. So the anger of the Most High was kindled against him.

The Most High sent a prophet who asked why he sought after gods that could not even deliver their own people out of his hand. This is why counsel is important. The prophet was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him and told him to forbear, be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said the Most High had determined to destroy him because he had done this and had not hearkened to counsel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Amaziah took advice and sent to Joash king of Israel saying, Come, let us see one another in the face. Joash answered with a parable of the thistle and the cedar, telling him his heart lifted him up to boast, and to abide at home rather than meddle to his hurt.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Amaziah would not hear, for it came of the Most High, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies because they had sought the gods of Edom. Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Joash took Amaziah, came to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem four hundred cubits. He took all the gold and silver and the vessels found in the house of the Most High, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria. The two kingdoms had real animosity, calling each other another nation, brother stealing the vessels out of his own brother's temple.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash king of Israel. From the time he turned away from following the Most High they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish, but they sent after him and slew him there.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

points: They brought him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah. When a man departs from the Most High, the protection departs with him.
